result.summary: Adds btck_chainstate_manager_set_clock_time to the kernel C API and introduces ChainstateManager::Now() as the single time-injection point across validation paths. Also moves NodeClock::now() into a separate file so libbitcoinkernel fails to link if nondeterministic clocks are called directly, and converts mempool timestamp fields to use chrono time points.
result.problem: Libbitcoinkernel consumers and multi-instance tests currently lack a way to set mock time on a specific ChainstateManager instance without altering global state or relying on the host system clock.

categories.rationale: Kernel consumers need to run validation deterministically without relying on process-global state. Merged PR #35496 already provided a basic global mock time for the kernel, so instance-scoped time is a valuable architectural refinement rather than an emergency blocker.

result.card: This pull request adds an API to set clock time on a ChainstateManager instance, allowing libbitcoinkernel consumers to validate blocks and headers deterministically without relying on system clocks or process-global state. It also moves nondeterministic clock calls into a separate source file so libbitcoinkernel cannot link against them, and updates mempool timestamp fields to use chrono time points. This improves upon the global mock time introduced in merged PR 35496 by scoping time to individual chainstate managers. Reviewers have helped refine chrono typing and test coverage, though a question from maflcko regarding whether this remains relevant after 35496 merged remains unanswered.
